entries.claim: Separate peg approach from risky low contact and active sweeps. Besides nudging a cube away during side transfer, a held peg can cross the cube's image band with little useful translation and leave it on the opposite side. Treat that visual response as failed engagement, not progress inferred from EE travel. Refresh stale cube grounding and recheck tool height, working span and side before another stroke.
entries.conditions: Revises the existing low-contact advice: retain ordinary duration-based budgets for unobstructed pickup/high approach; low approach/side transfer merits a single candidate review up to16 controls. For an active sweep with uncertain height/span or previous ineffective contact, prefer review within8 controls, and before a proposed opening transition. Earlier evidence under an80-control authorization showed away motion by+68, unmistakable by+75–80 with onset obscured. This episode used16 from502 and had a visible miss by about512 (+10, approximate); an8-control authorization from1022 showed opposite-side emergence by1028 (+6), yet its1030 wake was misinterpreted and another8 authorized. Eight is an earlier observation recommendation, not a demonstrated safe bound. Review must evaluate cube displacement; gripper guards cannot detect a miss. A before-command guard can catch release only, and should not block a demonstrated final release once arrival is supported.

entries.claim: When the current demonstration ends by releasing the peg after cube arrival, and current views support arrival, permit a matching near-static VLA release under close review even if official success is still false. Do not make success a prerequisite for executing the demonstrated finishing transition.
entries.conditions: MoveCube peg method, only after checking the current demonstration and actual cube/target relation; not permission to drop a tool while the cube is visibly off target.
